analyzed_vuln.description: `json_cquote` mishandles its destination capacity. It defines `endp = dest + len`, but when the output cursor reaches that one-past-the-allocation address its overflow branch writes `*dest = 0`, causing a one-byte heap-buffer-overflow. The issue is exposed by JSON serialization of the fixed-width pre-R13 `MENUEXT` field: `FIELD_TFF` routes it through string-oriented `FIELD_TFv`/`json_cquote`, while `json_cquote` scans until NUL rather than respecting the field's 46-byte source bound. Thus an unterminated fixed field can make it consume adjacent structure bytes and fill the destination. The crash itself is the erroneous out-of-bounds terminator write in `json_cquote`; this function must never write at `dest + len`, and fixed-width callers also need bounded-source handling.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The harness must decode an `AC...` DWG sufficiently successfully, randomly select JSON output (`case 3`), and enter pre-R13 header emission with `numheader_vars > 74`, reaching `FIELD_TFF(MENUEXT, 46, 0)`. The attacker-controlled 46-byte `MENUEXT` must lack a NUL and contain enough JSON-escaped bytes to fill the computed 277-byte allocation (`6 * 46 + 1`); subsequent adjacent bytes must also be nonzero so the unbounded source scan continues. In this PoV the 46 bytes expand to 276 output bytes, one adjacent byte advances the cursor to offset 277, and another nonzero byte causes the capacity branch to write a terminator at offset 277, exactly one byte past the allocation.
